newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures weaker in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures weaker in featureless trade.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended weaker across the board in extremely thin volume on Monday, in tandem with the weaker New York market on Friday, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to four yen per gram lower. Most-active August 1997 gold settled four yen lower at 1,339 yen per gram after trading narrowly.
Activity in the gold market was dominated by sporadic position-adjustment in line with the currency market.
Spot gold was quoted at $394.90/385.20 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $384.85/385.35 in New York on Friday.
Activity in the spot gold market was quiet.
"Sentiment in the spot gold may depend on whether producers will launch selling or hold back selling," an senior dealer of a foreign bank said.

In gold futures market, private investors still held on to their massive long positions due to recent static price movements, while short-covering by trade houses limited any price falls in the December contract, they said.
Platinum futures ended steady to firmer, while silver and palladium futures settled narrowly mixed in sluggish trade.
Traders said buying interest by private investors in the metals remained thin, amid a lack of fresh incentives and a dearth of clues from the currency market.
Platinum futures ranged from unchanged to two yen per gram firmer. Benchmark August was two yen up at 1,370 yen.
Silver futures ranged from 1.4 yen per 10 grams weaker to 0.8 yen firmer, with benchmark August ending 1.2 yen lower at 182.0 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from two yen per gram easier to two firmer. Benchmark August was one yen lower at 439 yen.
